expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Dak Prescott is in an elite spot as the Cardinals have allowed the most TD passes per game this season.  CeeDee Lamb is now leading the NFL with 81 total targets making him my favorite pairing by far.  They both will be popular, but there are enough lower-owned players to pair this combo with.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: One of the most profitable strategies at quarterback this season has been picking on the Cardinals. They are 31st in EPA allowed per dropback and 30th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks. The Cowboys have been so bad that they are only 6.5-point favorites at home. If this game stays competitive, Dak Prescott ($8,000 FD / $6,300 DK) should have a monster fantasy outing. His expected fantasy points per game of 21.1 is one of the highest of any quarterback on the slate. He’s easy to stack with too, as CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens have a combined 50% target share and 71% air yards share.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Dak Prescott is one of the top cash QBs on the board. He enters week 8 with a meeting with the Cardinals who have ranked bottom 5 vs opposing QBs this season. Cardinals allow the 3rd highest EPA/pass and the Cowboys are implied fort he highest total on the slate. Play with confidence.

players.notes: Top team total facing a secondary allowing the most passing touchdowns.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Lamar is fully healthy in a shootout with Josh Allen and a terrible Bills defense. He leads all qualified QBs in yards per attempt, and he trails only Josh Allen in fantasy points per drop back. Plus, we are getting a nice discount given his recent absence & he's not even popular.

players.notes: Elite dual-threat option with a massive 54.5 game total against Buffalo.
Strong passing volume expected as massive home favorites against Tennessee.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Dallas ranks 30th in pass DVOA, plays soft coverage, and has been vulnerable in the red zone. The expected pressure is very low, making this one of the cleanest pockets on the slate. Dallas has also allowed plenty of rushing production to opposing quarterbacks. At this point, just play every QB against Dallas until they prove otherwise.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: I'm trying to find value wherever I can on this slate. Brissett is one of the better value spots in a great matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Brissett week in and week out is probably lower owned than he should be given the game environments the Cardinals have been in so far this season. With Dak and the Cowboys pieces being slated to draw a good majority of the ownership in this game, flipping the script and playing Brissett in GPPs is very enticing. Dallas is 2nd in EPA/pass and bottom 10 in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

players.notes: Low-owned value option benefiting from a high-paced 54.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Josh Allen ($9,400 FD / $7,700 DK) has the highest floor/ceiling combo of any player in fantasy football. He’s scored at least 18 fantasy points in every game this season. More importantly, he’s topped 34 fantasy points in 3 of those games. When he has a ceiling performance, he typically doesn’t garner more than 10% ownership. With Lamar Jackson tentatively expected back this week, this game has serious shootout potential. The Ravens have allowed the 10th-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points to quarterbacks this season.

players.notes: Highest floor and ceiling combination in a game with a 54.5 total.
Solid dual-threat upside with a 20.1 projection at a modest salary.
Solid pass volume projection in a divisional matchup with a 45.5 total.
High pass-rate offense in a competitive divisional game against Minnesota.
Cheap salary with a solid 3.19 points per dollar projection vs Las Vegas.
Value quarterback option with a 25.7 ceiling against the Rams.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Tuten is 11th in the league in yards after contact per attempt, but his yards before contact have been poor, which should improve this week. His pass game utilization has been solid, and the Jags are 10 point home favorites against a tanking Colts team. The Colts run defense has been poor to this point (26th in success rate, 28th in EPA/rush), and they're 26th in yards before contact allowed. Then, they traded their best run stopper in DeForest Buckner this week, which creates an eruption spot for Tuten on the ground.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Bhayshul Tuten ($6,900 FD / $5,900 DK) isn’t a workhorse running back for the Jaguars, but he has clearly separated himself from the other backs on the roster. Over the last 3 games, he has touch counts of 16, 24, and 19. He’s seen 43% of the carries inside the 5-yard line and has run a route on 41% of dropbacks. More importantly, the Jaguars are large favorites at home against the Colts, who are 27th in EPA against the run and 27th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to running backs.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Love Tuten in all formats this week and I think his ownership continues to trend upwards as we approach slate lock on Sunday. Jaguars have the 4th highest implied team total and are 9.5 point favorites, which should imply a run script. Colts have already traded one of their defensive stars in DeForest Buckner and were already in the bottom 5 in EPA/run. The Colts also shipped out All-Pro OG Quenton Nelson which won't help this Colts offense staying on the field.

players.notes: Heavy touch volume as big home favorites against a struggling run defense.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Brown has been miserable with his efficiency but now gets to play the Titans and is top 10 amongst all RBs in expected fantasy points

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Don’t get me wrong, I like the expensive running backs this week. However, they have some of the toughest matchups on the slate. This could be a great slate to attack the mid-range running backs. Chase Brown ($7,100 FD / $6,300 DK) has yet to score more than 20 fantasy points in a game this season and has been held under 12 fantasy points in 4 of the last 5 games. While the game log isn’t encouraging, he has played on 71% of the snaps and should have his best game script to date. The Bengals are 10.5-point home favorites against the Titans, who are 24th in EPA against the run and 29th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to running backs.

players.notes: Massive 71 percent snap share as heavy home favorites against Tennessee.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Gibbs is expensive, but he is worth it as he is now leading the NFL in touches at 166.  This Lions/Vikings game is another game I want exposure to and even though he’s $9,500 on DK, I will be looking for cheaper receiving and TE options to make it work.

players.notes: Leads the NFL in total touches in a high-total divisional matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Coming off a 25 carry game, Williams' coaches spoke about how much the team has been trying to get back to the ground game and they now play a bottom 5 EPA/play defense.

players.notes: Coming off 25 carries to face a bottom-five EPA run defense.
Elite workhorse role with a massive 35.8 ceiling against Tampa Bay.
Strong projected workload as a seven-point home favorite over Miami.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: The Jets aren't bad defensively at all, but Jeanty has a very solid role in this offense. Even when he's not running the ball particularly well, he still has a major role in the passing game.

players.notes: Secure pass-catching role out of the backfield against the Jets.
Solid receiving upside in a closely contested divisional matchup.
Elite Bell-cow projection with a 31.2 ceiling against Denver.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Henry gets the return of Lamar Jackson which should help keep defenses a little more honest, which is no shot at Snoop Huntley who plays every well. The Bills defense allow the 4th most FPs to opposing RBs and Henry has historically had some crazy performances vs the kings of the AFC East. Henry's ownership should be in the single digits with the likes of Gibbs, Bijan, and Chase Brown on the slate.

players.notes: Benefits from Lamar Jackson returning to keep defenses honest.
Solid workhorse projection as a home favorite against the Chargers.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Zay has been one of the best WRs in the NFL this season despite missing time himself and playing multiple games with out Lamar. He leads the league in yards per route run and YAC, and his metrics are some of the most ridiculous you'll ever see when he has Lamar over Huntley. He's the closes thing to JSN/Puka, but he isn't priced accordingly.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Flowers has a 49% target per route run rate with Lamar Jackson at QB, and the Bills didn't have an answer for Puka Nacua or Amon-Ra St. Brown.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Zay Flowers is having an upreal 2026 and gets Lamar Jackson back at QB. The Bills have also allowed the most FPs to opposing WRs and are 4th in EPA/Pass. The Ravens have the 5th highest implied team total and the highest of any of the road teams (Pats are close behind). With Lamar in the lineup, Zay averages about a 42% target share and close to 8 yards per route run.

players.notes: Elite 49 percent target per route run rate with Lamar Jackson at quarterback.
Leading the NFL in targets in an elite spot against Arizona.
Strong deep role and red-zone usage as a massive home favorite.
Strong slot role and target floor in a high-total game environment.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Puka Nacua ($9,100 FD / $8,600 DK) should be one of the most popular players on the slate. With Davante Adams out, he’s going to soak up even more targets than usual. And that’s saying something since he already owns a 32% target share and a 41% air yards share. The Rams’ offense hasn’t exactly been dominant this season, so I could see Sean McVay keeping his foot on the gas even if they are playing with a lead. The Chargers have been middling against the pass, but they are 20th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

players.notes: Soaking up extra targets with a 32 percent share and 41 percent air yards.
Strong target volume with a 31.3 ceiling against Tampa Bay.
Part of a lethal 50 percent combined target share stack against Arizona.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: In the 11 dropbacks that Baker Mayfield DID have against the Panthers before the blowout began, Godwin had a 45% target share. That obvioiusly won't hold but with no Egbuka, he is the primary weapon.

players.notes: Primary weapon in the passing game with a massive target share.
Elite target volume and ceiling as a heavy home favorite.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Wilson is fairly-priced, in a nice matchup. This is a squeaky wheel ready for some grease.

players.notes: Fairly priced in a squeaky-wheel matchup against Las Vegas.
Solid perimeter role in a game with the highest total on the slate.
Deep threat upside with a 22.4 ceiling against Kansas City.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Dolphins are 31st in yards per target allowed to TEs, and AJ Brown now appears to be trending towards not playing with his knee flaring up, alongside Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Dolphins continue to struggle vs the TE position, again bottom 3 in fantasy points allowed vs the position. With AJ Brown injured, expect both Henry and Raridon to be utilized more. Tight ends have seen close to 30% of targets and 30% of fantasy points allowed by Miami. I would play Henry in all formats, but wouldn't fault you to mix in some Raridon in large field MME.

players.notes: Facing a defense allowing nearly 30 percent of targets to tight ends.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Hockenson has the most receptions of any player with Kyler Murray on the field and is going up against a Lions team that's allowed the most yards and 10 total TDs to TEs this year.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Detroit has allowed ten total TD’s to TE’s this year, which is the most in the NFL.  Hockenson has been very efficient catching 27 of his 32 targets and I love pairing Hockenson with Gibbs to get exposure to this game.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Tight ends vs Lions continue to deliver on the year. They have allowed a league-high 10 TDs already; to put that into perspective, only 7 teams allowed 10+ TDs in 17 games last year. While the Vikings have had their struggles scoring, at least Hockenson is getting his looks in the redzone. Hockenson leads the team with 7 redzone targets, with the next best being Jetta with 5.

players.notes: Leads the team in red-zone targets against a defense allowing ten tight end.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: One of the reasons why I am looking to save a bit at running back is because I want as much exposure to Trey McBride ($7,300 FD / $7,400 DK) as possible. He’s essentially a WR1 that we get to target at tight end. He owns a 27% target share and a 23% air yards share this season, and he is facing the Cowboys, who are 30th in EPA allowed per dropback. The game script looks great as well, as the Cardinals are 6.5-point underdogs on the road.

players.notes: Operating as a primary receiver with a 27 percent target share against Dallas.
Strong route participation and red-zone upside against Atlanta.
Elite seam usage in a high-total matchup against Buffalo.
Elite target monster at tight end with a 28.1 ceiling.
High route rate and seam usage in a 54.5 total shootout.
Strong red-zone role in a high-paced divisional matchup.
Reliable target floor and red-zone usage against Denver.
